title: Finite systems, states and basis labels
objectives: Choose a finite state set appropriate to a modelling question.
Translate a definite state into a labelled standard basis vector.
Distinguish coordinate dimension from binary storage size.

quizzes.question: If we reorder the coordinates, does the same switch setting necessarily keep the same column vector?
options: Yes: coordinate order has no effect.
No: the coordinates can change while the labelled setting stays the same.
No: reordering physically changes the setting.
feedback: The position of the 1 depends on which coordinate corresponds to the setting.
Correct. A vector must be interpreted with its declared basis order.
Changing our coordinate convention does not operate on the physical device.

quizzes.question: What is the minimum fixed-length binary storage for five distinct labels?
feedback: Two bits provide only four distinct strings.
Correct. Three bits provide eight strings; three are unused in a five-label code.
Five one-hot coordinates are one representation, but they are not the minimum number of storage bits.

source: Lecture Slides - 1 to 7.pdf, PDF pp.3–4. The introductory July 26 lecture transcript informs the systems-first explanation; classroom dialogue is paraphrased rather than published.
prerequisites: Basic arithmetic and elementary algebra. A matrix-multiplication refresher is included before composition.
